text:
Your na yin element is Shan Tou Huo — fire on the mountaintop, bright and visible from far away. Fire is fed by wood and strengthened by more fire, so names carrying wood or fire energy suit you best. Food and drink as an industry sits on fire (the kitchen) and water (beverages). Fire is a natural fit for you; water is the element that dampens fire, so it is better kept as an accent than as the core of the name.

Here are 12 name ideas for your company:

### Group 1: Plain English (warm, easy to remember)

**Hearth & Table** — Meaning: the fireplace at the centre of the home, and the table around it · Element: Fire · Why it fits: the hearth is fire at its most welcoming — the same element as yours · Practical note: works well for a family restaurant or comfort-food concept.

**Timber Kitchen** — Meaning: a kitchen built from solid wood · Element: Wood · Why it fits: wood feeds fire, giving your energy a steady supply · Practical note: suits rustic, open-kitchen or wood-fired formats.

**Ember Lane** — Meaning: a street lit by glowing embers · Element: Fire · Why it fits: keeps the fire theme but in a gentle, inviting way · Practical note: good for a neighbourhood bistro or wine bar.

**The Orchard Room** — Meaning: a room surrounded by fruit trees · Element: Wood · Why it fits: living wood that keeps your fire burning · Practical note: fits brunch, bakery-cafe or seasonal menus.

---

### Group 2: Classical, Sino-inspired (formal, good for registration)

**Yanlin Holdings** — Meaning: from 炎 (flame) and 林 (forest) · Element: Fire, Wood · Why it fits: wood and fire together — the most direct match for your chart · Practical note: a solid parent-company name for several restaurant brands.

**Mingtai Foods** — Meaning: 明 (bright) and 泰 (prosperous, peaceful) · Element: Fire · Why it fits: brightness is the nature of your mountaintop fire · Practical note: works for food manufacturing or wholesale lines later.

**Songbai Group** — Meaning: 松柏, pine and cypress — evergreen, enduring · Element: Wood · Why it fits: long-lasting wood to keep the fire going · Practical note: conveys stability to banks and suppliers.

**Huiguang Dining** — Meaning: 輝光, radiant light · Element: Fire · Why it fits: echoes the visibility of fire on a mountaintop · Practical note: fits an upscale dining brand.

---

### Group 3: Blended modern (built for chains and delivery)

**Flame & Fern** — Meaning: fire and green leaves together · Element: Fire, Wood · Why it fits: wood feeding fire, in two short words · Practical note: easy to turn into a logo and memorable on delivery apps.

**Pinewood Grill** — Meaning: a grill fired with pine · Element: Wood, Fire · Why it fits: the classic wood-to-fire chain in one name · Practical note: ready-made for a barbecue or grill concept.

**Sunpeak Eats** — Meaning: sunlight on the summit · Element: Fire · Why it fits: a modern take on "fire on the mountaintop" · Practical note: suits fast-casual and takeaway.

**Copper Ember** — Meaning: glowing embers in a copper pan · Element: Fire, Metal · Why it fits: fire leads, and the metal it shapes is traditionally read as wealth · Practical note: fits a cocktail bar or open-kitchen restaurant.

---

*Note: the element of a name is a supportive, symbolic layer for your brand. A restaurant's success still depends most on food quality, location and how carefully you manage cash flow.*
